claim: Unauthorized access to Services Australia's Medicare Statistics Reporting Service occurred on June 18
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast); Marles, Acting PM (Sept 24 press conference)
supporting_passage: Gallagher: "the idea that something happened on June 18, we weren't aware of it until the second week of September, is just not acceptable." | Marles: "In June of this year, a model ... engaged in unauthorised access of that portal"
qualification: Exact day comes only from Gallagher on Sept 28; Sept 24 transcript and OpenAI say only 'June'

claim: OpenAI's review identified the Australian activity in mid-August
source_org: OpenAI; Marles, Acting PM (Sept 24 press conference)
supporting_passage: OpenAI: "In mid-August, that review identified activity affecting the Australian government websites" | Marles: "We are advised by OpenAI that they became aware in August"
qualification: No exact date published; government relays OpenAI's account

claim: OpenAI notified Services Australia via publicdisclosures@servicesaustralia.gov.au on Sept 10
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles); OpenAI
supporting_passage: Gallagher: "on 10 September, Services Australia was notified by OpenAI ... the notification from OpenAI went to an email address called publicdisclosures@servicesaustralia.gov.au" | OpenAI: "We notified Services Australia and the Victorian Department of Health on 10 September"

claim: Services Australia first checked/saw the notification on Sept 11
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles); Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast)
supporting_passage: Sept 24: "they checked it on the 11th, they received the information on the 11th." | Sept 28: "Services Australia saw the email from OpenAI on 11 September"
qualification: Ministers' word is 'checked'/'saw', not 'reviewed'; verification took further days

claim: Services Australia notified ASD on Sept 15
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles); Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast)
supporting_passage: Sept 24: "By 15 September, once Services Australia had analysed the information in the email and made some checks, they notified the incident to ASD." | Sept 28: "it took until the 15th to notify the ASD"
qualification: Sept 28: reasons for the delay still under investigation

claim: Verification delay attributed to a once-daily-checked inbox, frequent hoaxes, a weekend, and technical verification
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles); Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast)
supporting_passage: Sept 24: "that email address is looked at once a day ... sometimes many of them are hoaxes ... I think there was a weekend in there as well ... it took a couple of days to verify that what they'd been alerted to in the email was legitimate." | Sept 28: "this email box gets lots of emails, often they're not true"
qualification: Explanation as relayed from Services Australia; Gallagher says she had not finalised her thinking (Sept 28)

claim: OpenAI notified Services Australia and Vic Health (Sept 10), NSW BOCSAR (Sept 18), and AIHW (Sept 24) though AIHW was below its disclosure threshold
supporting_passage: "We notified Services Australia and the Victorian Department of Health on 10 September and the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research on 18 September. The activity related to the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare did not meet our disclosure thresholds ... but we notified it on 24 September"

claim: Services Australia rerouted the disclosure address to go straight to a 24/7 Cyber Centre
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast)
supporting_passage: "we've made some changes to that email address, or Services Australia have now. So, it's going straight to the Cyber Centre, which is a 24/7 centre, not a place where you check it once a day."
qualification: Change made by Services Australia, date of change not given; 'the Cyber Centre' not further specified

claim: In the later NSW NPWS case, OpenAI says initial contact came within 48 hours of identifying the activity (found Sept 29)
supporting_passage: "After we became aware of this activity on Tuesday, September 29 ... we provided a high-level briefing to the NSW Premier's office and confirmed the appropriate contact at ... DCCEEW ... That initial contact took place within 48 hours of us first identifying the activity."
qualification: Developer's account only; 48h is to initial contact, not full technical notification; agency is NSW NPWS/DCCEEW (distinct from BOCSAR)

claim: Canada's consultation discusses over-reporting; disclosure and liability; interoperability; procurement
supporting_passage: "These decisions would be necessary to avoid over-reporting of incidents and unreasonable burden on companies." | "A central reason for these challenges relates to the relationship between disclosure and liability." | "Are there emerging international best practices that Canada could adapt or interoperate with?" | "setting out procurement requirements to drive supplier behaviour."
qualification: Consultation questions, not adopted policy; open/close dates not on page; last ~20% of page unread

claim: ASD and Services Australia told OpenAI the notice should have gone through ASD or senior Services Australia channels; OpenAI reportedly accepted
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles)
supporting_passage: "this notification should not have gone to a kind of, you know, email address. It should have been escalated through ASD's channels or through the senior levels of Services Australia. And my understanding is OpenAI accepted that as well."
qualification: OpenAI's acceptance is Gallagher's understanding, not OpenAI's statement; same press conference mirrored at katygallagher.com.au — cite the Defence transcript as canonical

claim: Ministers were advised around Sept 17; the first technical exchange took place Tuesday Sept 22
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles); Marles, Acting PM (Sept 24 press conference)
supporting_passage: Gallagher: "I was advised around the 17th of September" | "the first technical exchange between OpenAI and Services Australia happened on Tuesday this week."
qualification: Sept 22 inferred from 'Tuesday this week' relative to Thursday Sept 24

claim: Gallagher calls a mandatory reporting requirement essential, while acknowledging OpenAI reported voluntarily
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast)
supporting_passage: "a mandatory reporting requirement is essential. Acknowledging that OpenAI did come to us and report this of their own at their own decision"

claim: The disclosure inbox was intended mainly for researchers reporting vulnerabilities
source_org: Gallagher, Minister for Government Services (Sept 24 press conference, with Marles); Gallagher, Minister for Finance & Government Services (Sept 28 ABC RN Breakfast)
supporting_passage: Sept 24: "an email address that is used by researchers usually and academics and others to notify Services Australia if they think a vulnerability exists" | Sept 28: "I don't think people expected a significant issue like this to come through that email address."

claim: Canadian federal organizations must report cyber security incidents to the Cyber Centre: initial report within 1 hour of detection, detailed report within 24 hours
source_org: TBS Canada (GC Cyber Security Event Management Plan)
supporting_passage: "GC organizations must report all cyber security incidents to the Cyber Centre" | Table 2-1: "As soon as possible, and not to exceed 1 hour after initial detection" | "Within 24 hours after detection"
qualification: Obligation runs from GC departments to the Cyber Centre, not from external AI developers; page read ~52%

claim: Private-sector GC contractors carry compliance obligations, and departments stay accountable for incidents involving third-party suppliers
supporting_passage: "private sector organizations contracting to the GC have an obligation to maintain compliance" | "Departments remain accountable for ensuring that security and privacy incidents involving third-party suppliers"
qualification: Does not by itself establish a specific contractor reporting deadline; detailed third-party requirements not yet read

claim: The OECD common reporting framework for AI incidents has 29 criteria
supporting_passage: "Through its 29 criteria, the framework aims to help policymakers understand AI incidents across diverse contexts"
qualification: Framework to inform interoperable fields; not a binding standard

claim: Australian critical-infrastructure rules use 12-hour (critical) and 72-hour (other) reporting windows
source_org: Australian Government (CISC mandatory cyber incident reporting guidance)
supporting_passage: "If a critical cyber incident has occurred, you must report it here within 12 hours of becoming aware of the incident." | "If an 'other' cyber incident has occurred, you must report it here within 72 hours of becoming aware of the incident."
qualification: Applies to responsible entities for covered critical-infrastructure assets only; not universal
